newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 26.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - While Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus spoke out yesterday against a referendum for entry of the Czech Republic into NATO, officials of the strongest opposition party, the Social Democrats (CSSD) insist that a referendum is necessary.

- In the tender for Aero Vodochody, CTK said yesterday that only Cimex Holding remained in the contest, but that there are still other interested parties. According to the information, Boeing and CSA were ruled out of the tender, and Lockheed Martin and British Aerospace and Saab did not apply.

- The Finance Ministry and the Trade Ministry are preparing two different concepts for privatisation of energy companies, and the ministers in charge, Ivan Kocarnik and Vladimir Dlouhy, do not know the contents of each other's proposals.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Just before the beginning of a conference which should address the problem of how and by how much to increase energy prices and rents, the participants in the conference are nearing an agreement. While the dominant opinion is to increase rents before energy prices, one of the most important coalition parties, ODS, prefers energy price increases first.

- The state will soon sell Karlovy Vary Becherovka, and the company, which is one of the last Czech gems, will most probably stay home. The state decided to offer the liqueur company to domestic owners, which could obtain 51 percent of shares in a tender, and foreign investors should be able to obtain another 38 percent of shares.
PRAVO - The decline of the crown by five to six percent is more weakening within the fluctuation zone than a devaluation, a spokesman for the Czech National Bank, Martin Svehla, said on Tuesday.

- An indefinite strike began in Poldi Steel on Tuesday morning, because employees have not received wages for a few months now. If wages are not paid to all employees by February 13, the union will file a legal suit against the management.

- The vice-chairman of the cabinet and chairman of the Christian Democratic Union (KDU-CSL), Josef Lux, does not want to apologise to the former head of the secret service (BIS), Stanislav Devaty. He wants the apology for false accusations that the BIS was cooperating with the Interior Ministry in observing politicians.

LIDOVE NOVINY - UNISYS and IDOM, which were originally disqualified from the public tender for a four million crown staff information system for the Czech Army, were reentered into the competition by the Defence Ministry on the basis of a legal analysis.
